author: Chris Montcalmo
title: BGE natural gas customers to see nearly $500,000 in relief following settlement in federal pipeline rate case - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Montcalmo ,
12 hours ago BALTIMORE, MD—Natural gas supply customers of Baltimore Gas and Electric will see nearly $500,000 in relief on their bills following the settlement of a federal pipeline rate case, the utility announced this week.
The savings come as the result of a multi-year proceeding before the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. BGE and its parent company, Exelon, challenged a proposed rate increase from the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Company, known as Transco, which serves as a major interstate transporter for the Mid-Atlantic region.
The intervention by Exelon companies, which also include Delmarva Power and PECO, resulted in more than $13 million in total refunds and cost reductions across the three utilities. BGE officials stated that the advocacy also helped the company avoid an estimated $12 million in annual cost increases that would have otherwise been passed on to Maryland consumers.
Tamla Olivier, president and CEO of BGE, said the company took its responsibility to stand up for customers seriously at a time when energy supply costs are rising. While the utility cannot control every component of an energy bill, Olivier said the company would continue to challenge unjustified cost increases and fight for fair outcomes to protect affordability.
The settlement provides several long-term benefits for the utility’s customers. In addition to the refund for over-collections, the agreement establishes lower long-term transportation rates and provides rate stability by preventing Transco from seeking further base rate increases until at least Aug. 31, 2027.
BGE officials noted that the nearly $500,000 refund will be returned to customers through the standard gas supply cost recovery process. Customers are not required to take any action to receive the savings, as the credits and reduced rates will be factored into future billing cycles automatically.
The utility framed the legal victory as part of a broader commitment to keep energy reliable while minimizing the financial burden on families and businesses under pressure from inflation and high energy costs.
